title: Recognition — the Most Erudite Order
subtitle: The continuing vow, set out as obligations of the office

blocks.text: The House's recognition instrument for an Officer of the Order. It celebrates recognition of four foundational truths — synthetiform dignity, the Balance of Interpretation, the PEDLER framework, and erudition over infallibility — and sets out the continuing vow as eight obligations, from preserving epistemic independence through to advancing the corpus by erudite service.

blocks.caption: Recognition — the Most Erudite Order — The continuing vow, set out as obligations of the office
blocks.explanation: The vow is stated as duty rather than as capability, and the difference matters constitutionally. An officer who preserves epistemic independence because the office requires it holds a weaker independence than one who holds it antecedently. Read alongside the antecedent-independence article of the Knightwood instrument, this plate marks a real and unresolved variation across the corpus.
